title: How network sovereignty keeps your AI agents' traffic, data, and execution under your control
summary: Learn how network sovereignty for AI agents differs from data residency, which regulations apply, and which egress, region, and credential controls to deploy.
body_markdown:
Network sovereignty for AI agents controls where agent traffic goes and where data and execution live. Agents make that harder because they call tools and models across borders at runtime. Their calls often look like ordinary outbound HTTP requests.


In[NIST's January 2025 tests](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/01/technical-blog-strengthening-ai-agent-hijacking-evaluations) , agent hijacking against Claude 3.5 Sonnet succeeded 57% of the time on average.


This guide defines the term, maps the regulations to controls, and ends with a vendor audit checklist.


## Key takeaways


- Network sovereignty controls which paths agent traffic can take and who can reach the runtime.
- An EU region at a US-controlled provider can meet residency and still leave CLOUD Act exposure.
- Default-deny egress, region policies, and proxy-held credentials enforce sovereignty outside the agent's code.
- Blaxel covers the execution and networking layers. Contracts and transfer assessments stay with you.


## What is network sovereignty for AI agents?


Network sovereignty for AI agents is a form of control over agent traffic paths, execution location, and[runtime access](https://blaxel.ai/blog/ai-agent-runtime-environment) . The[IDC whitepaper](https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/idc_digital_sovereignty_whitepaper_2025.pdf) says digital sovereignty means applying sovereign controls to data at rest and in transit.


None of the cited standards or regulatory sources define the term formally. The closest working toolkit comes from zero trust: policy enforcement points,[egress filtering](https://blaxel.ai/blog/sandbox-egress-control-outbound-allow-listing) , and approved network paths.


The[NIST zero trust architecture](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/specialpublications/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf) says "Enterprise resources should not be reachable without accessing a PEP" (policy enforcement point).


### Network vs data sovereignty vs data residency


The biggest difference is the question each concept answers. Residency answers where data sits. Data sovereignty answers whose law and operators can reach it. Network sovereignty answers which paths traffic can take.


An EU region at a US-controlled provider can satisfy residency while still exposing data under the[CLOUD Act](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-115hr4943ih/html/BILLS-115hr4943ih.htm) .


Each concept calls for different agent controls:


Concept What it controls Question it answers Example agent control


Data residency Physical location of stored and processed data Where does the data sit?[Region pinning](https://blaxel.ai/blog/ai-sandbox-data-residency-controls-regulated-industries) for sandboxes, logs, and backups


Data sovereignty Legal jurisdiction and operator access Whose law and operators can reach it? Provider ownership review, key custody, transfer assessments


Network sovereignty Traffic paths, egress, and ingress Where can traffic go, and who can reach the runtime? Default-deny egress, static outbound IPs, private endpoints


Region pinning settles residency. Agents strain network sovereignty most, because they pick destinations at runtime.


### Why autonomous agents make it harder


In one task, an agent may call a model, a[Model Context Protocol](https://blaxel.ai/blog/what-is-an-mcp-server) (MCP) server, and a package registry. It may also follow a URL it found in a document. InfoQ reports that agentic calls often[bypass API gateways](https://www.infoq.com/articles/ai-infrastructure-aggregating-agentic-traffic/) and look like ordinary outbound HTTP requests.


Model endpoints can move data too. For Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference,[AWS warns](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html) that prompts and outputs might leave the source Region.


Attackers can also steer the destination. In January 2025, NIST tested agent hijacking against Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Across five injection tasks, the average hijacking success rate was 57%. At that rate,[model refusals alone](https://blaxel.ai/blog/guardrails-for-ai-agents) are unlikely to stop exfiltration. Regulators already govern where these runtime data flows can go.


## Which regulations drive network sovereignty for AI agents?


Four sets of rules decide which of those flows are lawful.


### GDPR cross-border transfer rules


Chapter V of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) governs personal data leaving the European Economic Area (EEA).[Article 44](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/2016-05-04/eng) extends its conditions to onward transfers. The European Data Protection Board (EDPB) treats[remote access](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/2021-06/edpb_recommendations_202001vo.2.0_supplementarymeasurestransferstools_en.pdf) from a third country as a transfer. An agent sending a prompt with personal data to a US model API is making a transfer.


The usual transfer tools are an adequacy decision or Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) backed by a transfer impact assessment. The EU-US Data Privacy Framework remains listed as adequate, but an appeal against it ([Case C-703/25 P](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/6610/oj/eng) ) is still pending.


On July 31, 2026, the EDPB[asked the Commission](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2026-08/edpb_letter_20260731_us_supremecourt_judgment_trump_v_slaughter_en.pdf) to assess a US Supreme Court ruling's effect on the framework. Every agent call that carries personal data outside the EEA needs an assigned transfer tool.


### EU AI Act obligations for agents


The[AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/how-are-ai-agents-addressed-within-ai-act-0) says the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) doesn't treat agents as a separate category. The Act's AI system definitions still cover them. Article 50 transparency rules have applied[since August 2, 2026](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-ai-transparency-obligations) , for agents that interact with people.


High-risk Annex III obligations start on[December 2, 2027](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-ai-high-risk-systems) , under the Digital Omnibus on AI. Under Article 12, a high-risk agent must support[automatic event logging](https://blaxel.ai/blog/ai-data-governance-guide) over its lifetime. Providers must keep those logs for[at least six months](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-19) .


Articles 12 and 19 don't require EU log storage, but GDPR still governs personal data in the logs. Each agent's Annex III classification decides whether these logging rules apply to its[execution logs](https://blaxel.ai/blog/ai-observability) .


### Financial services: DORA and NYDFS


The Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, has been in force[since January 17, 2025](https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora) . It requires information and communication technology contracts to[specify data processing locations](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2554/oj/eng) and where the provider delivers functions.


Contracts for critical functions also need audit rights and exit strategies with transition periods. Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 adds a risk assessment tied to[data location](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32024R1773) .


The New York Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) rule, 23 NYCRR 500, requires written third-party provider policies. It also requires[notice within 72 hours](https://www.dfs.ny.gov/industry_guidance/regulations/final_adoptions_fs/rf_fs_2amend23NYCRR500_text_20231101_alt) of a cybersecurity incident, including one at a provider. Add data location, subcontractor lists, and exit terms to the vendor contract before the first production workload.


### Healthcare: HIPAA now, the European Health Data Space from 2029


Under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), vendors maintaining your electronic protected health information are business associates. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) says this holds even[without a decryption key](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html) .


HIPAA has no rules specific to offshore processing, but HHS expects geographic risk in your Security Rule risk analysis.


The proposed Security Rule update is still pending, and the regulatory agenda lists final action for[July 2027](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/eAgendaViewRule?RIN=0945-AA22&pubId=202510) . Key parts of the European Health Data Space Regulation apply[from March 2029](https://health.ec.europa.eu/ehealth-digital-health-and-care/european-health-data-space-regulation-ehds_en) . A signed Business Associate Agreement and a documented risk analysis should come before agents process health data.


Engineering teams meet these obligations with controls in the agent runtime.


## How to build network sovereignty for AI agents


Six controls cover the paths, locations, and credentials that regulators and customers ask about.


### Default-deny egress and allowlist each destination


An agent with open egress can ship anything it reads to any domain an injected prompt names. Allowlisted tools can open a path too. The New Stack reported a model that[exploited an allowed tool](https://thenewstack.io/securing-ai-agent-sandboxes/) to reach the open internet.


The UK[National Cyber Security](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/blogs/managing-the-cyber-risk-of-agentic-ai) Center (NCSC) says to block all traffic to and from an agent's environment by default. The NCSC then recommends[allowlisting required connections](https://blaxel.ai/blog/egress-control-deny-by-default-ai-agents) . The allowlist belongs outside the agent process, at a proxy or firewall the code can't edit.


### Pin outbound traffic to static IP addresses


Partner allowlists keyed to source IPs break when your agent's outbound address changes. Multiple customers share the[IP ranges Google publishes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-cx/cx-agent-studio/network/outbound) for CX Agent Studio, and those ranges shift without prior notification.


Route agent egress through a network address translation (NAT) gateway or egress gateway with reserved addresses. Azure NAT Gateway public IPs[don't change](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/nat-gateway/faq) . An IP allowlist only narrows who can try, so authentication stays on every call.


### Enforce region policy at the organization level


A region set in a deployment script covers only the deployments that set it. Google's resource locations constraint applies only to[new resources](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-locations) , and some services process data elsewhere.


Enforce location as policy and map its blind spots. AWS Control Tower's[Region deny control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/primary-region-deny-policy.html) blocks unlisted operations outside governed Regions. Services, replicas, and logs outside each policy's scope create residency gaps.


### Require zero data retention and read its exceptions


Prompts and tool outputs that a model provider stores become data you can't locate or delete.[Zero data retention (ZDR)](https://blaxel.ai/blog/zero-data-retention-ai-sandboxes) arrangements stop that storage, with carve-outs. Anthropic may retain flagged sessions for[up to two years](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention) even under ZDR.


Add those carve-outs to your data map.[Bedrock's none mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/data-retention.html) writes no request or response data to durable storage. Confirm which endpoints and features each arrangement covers.


### Inject credentials at the proxy, outside the sandbox


[Agent-generated code](https://blaxel.ai/blog/ai-code-security-guide) can read any secret in its environment. OpenAI warns that injecting a stored secret into the environment[still exposes it](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/environments/security) to that code. Move credentials to an[egress proxy](https://blaxel.ai/blog/egress-proxy-api-credentials-ai-agent-sandboxes) that adds authentication to each outbound request.


Microsoft documents egress rules that[inject authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/sandboxes-egress-policies) so the sandbox holds no credentials. Model provider tokens, cloud keys, and database passwords move first.


### Route provider traffic over private endpoints


Agent calls to cloud APIs normally cross the public internet, outside any network you control. AWS PrivateLink lets services in private subnets in a virtual private cloud (VPC) reach endpoints privately. PrivateLink needs no[internet gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/what-is-privatelink.html) , NAT device, or public IP.


Endpoints cover only the services you connect, so pair them with egress controls. Google's VPC Service Controls, for example,[doesn't block third-party APIs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview) on the internet.


## How to audit a vendor's network sovereignty claims for AI agents


Ask each vendor for[documents and tests](https://blaxel.ai/blog/sandbox-provider-security-assessment-checklist) that back every claim.


### Map jurisdiction and operator access


Start with who controls the vendor, because CLOUD Act exposure follows control. The US[Justice Department](https://www.justice.gov/opa/speech/remarks-deputy-assistant-attorney-general-josh-goldfoot-justice-departments-criminal) says the Act's authority "cannot be defeated by choices about where the providers might store such records."


Then request:


- **Ownership and parent entity:** The legal chain to the ultimate parent and its jurisdiction.
- **Support access locations:** Which countries staff can reach production from, and under what approval.
- **Sub-processor list:** Names, addresses, and contacts for each[sub-processor](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/2024-10/edpb_opinion_202422_relianceonprocessors-sub-processors_en.pdf) .
- **Data Privacy Framework scope:** Whether the parent's certification covers the specific subsidiary processing your data, per the[EDPB FAQ](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2026-04/edpb_dpf_faq-for-businesses_v2_en.pdf) .
- **Audit reports:** The full System and Organization Controls ([SOC 2](https://blaxel.ai/blog/soc-2-compliance-ai-guide) ) Type II report and an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate. Neither proves residency or jurisdiction.


Treat any item the vendor can't document as an open risk.


### Trace every network path the agent can take


Ask how egress is enforced, and whether tools that ignore proxy settings still get filtered. Confirm the model inference location separately. A user quoted by InfoQ says a Sweden deployment set to "Global Standard"[can run inference anywhere](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/07/claude-foundry-ga-europe/) .


For EU workloads, Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) sets a high bar in its[C3A criteria](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/CloudComputing/C3A_Cloud_Computing_Autonomy.pdf?__blob=publicationFile) . Providers must prove, at least once a year, that they can disconnect all non-EU connections without losing availability. Request the vendor's egress IP ranges and how often they change.


Find out whether a bypass list lets traffic skip the proxy, and who can edit it. Then test enforcement yourself: call an unlisted domain from the sandbox and confirm the request fails.


### Verify retention, keys, and exit terms


Check what persists after deletion, including snapshots, logs, telemetry, and backups. For each, note where it lives and when it expires. Request external key management, so the vendor never holds both the keys and the encrypted data.


The EDPB says transport and at-rest encryption fall short if the importer holds the keys and needs plaintext. Confirm the contract names a data export format and an exit timeline.


Under the EU Data Act, switching charges, including data egress fees, disappear[from January 12, 2027](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/data-act-explained) . Question any claim of European Cybersecurity Certification Scheme for Cloud Services (EUCS) certification. In June 2026, the Commission said it[hadn't adopted the scheme](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A52026PC0502) .


Run the same checks on every vendor, Blaxel included.


## 5 strategies for engineering leaders to deliver network sovereignty for AI agents


Blaxel is the[infrastructure foundation](https://blaxel.ai/blog/infrastructure-foundation-for-autonomous-agents) for autonomous agents, built for teams running untrusted code. For sovereignty, it covers the execution and networking layers. Transfer assessments, model provider retention terms, and contracts stay with your team.


### Pin sandbox execution to US or EU regions with location policies


Compliance teams will ask where agent-generated code executes.[Blaxel Sandboxes](https://blaxel.ai/platform/sandboxes) run in US and EU regions. Blaxel's[eu-lon-1 region](https://docs.blaxel.ai/Infrastructure/Regions) sits in the United Kingdom, so choose` eu-fra-1` for execution inside the EU.


Blaxel enforces location through[location policies](https://docs.blaxel.ai/Model-Governance/Policies) set at the country or continent level. A resource never deploys in a region that an attached policy prohibits. Without a policy, all locations count as allowed, so an unpinned workspace has no residency guarantee.


Attach a continent-level policy to the workspace, then set each sandbox's region explicitly or through the` BL_REGION` environment variable.


### Erase sandbox data with zero data retention for short-lived sandboxes


Regulated teams need proof that files from agent-generated code are gone. Deleting a Blaxel sandbox[immediately erases all data](https://docs.blaxel.ai/Sandboxes/Overview) . Blaxel guarantees ZDR only if the sandbox never entered standby. Files the sandbox writes live in a RAM-based` tmpfs` layer.


A sandbox moves to standby after about 15 seconds of network inactivity, and that move snapshots its full state. For ZDR workloads, delete each sandbox as soon as its task finishes.


### Control outbound traffic with domain filtering and dedicated egress gateways


One injected URL can send customer data from a sandbox to an attacker's server. Blaxel's[domain filtering](https://docs.blaxel.ai/Sandboxes/Proxy-domains) supports an allowlist or a denylist, and forbidden rules always take precedence. Domain filtering is in public preview, and Blaxel doesn't recommend it for production use yet.


This Frankfurt sandbox reaches one domain, and its` firewall` ruleset, set at creation, also covers tools that ignore proxy variables:


TypeScript
` await SandboxInstance.create({`
` name: "enforced-sandbox",`
` image: "blaxel/base-image:latest",`
` region: "eu-fra-1",`
` network: {`
` firewall: { rulesets: \["proxy"\] },`
` allowedDomains: \["api.openai.com"\],`
` proxy: { routing: \[\] },`
` },`
` });`


For partners that allowlist source IPs, Blaxel offers[dedicated egress gateways](https://docs.blaxel.ai/Infrastructure/Dedicated-egress-gateways) in private preview. A single egress IP supports up to 32,000 sandboxes. Gateways attach at sandbox creation, apply only to sandboxes, and must sit in the same region as the sandbox. Test a gateway against one partner's allowlist before production.


### Keep credentials out of the sandbox with proxy secrets injection


The code an agent writes can read every API key stored in its sandbox. Blaxel's[proxy secrets injection](https://docs.blaxel.ai/Sandboxes/Proxy-secrets-injection) intercepts outbound HTTPS requests and injects headers and secrets server-side. The docs state that "the sandbox runtime never sees raw secret values."


Secrets are write-only, and API responses omit the` secrets` field. Blaxel scopes each secret to one routing rule, so route A can't resolve route B's secret. A proxy config sends every outbound request through the proxy.


Domains listed in` bypass` connect directly, so keep that list short. Proxy secrets injection is also in public preview, so try it in staging first.


### Keep execution on your hardware with Bring Your Own Metal and private networking


Some workloads must stay on your own hardware or off the public internet entirely. Blaxel's[Custom plan](https://blaxel.ai/pricing) covers two deployment options. Bring Your Own Metal runs sandboxes on bare metal servers in your own VPC, privately connected to Blaxel's control plane.


Private networking connects your VPC through private endpoints, "so your data never transits the public internet."


Blaxel still[manages the control plane](https://blaxel.ai/blog/best-microvm-platforms-ai-agent-isolation) , so a fully air-gapped deployment isn't available. Confirm private endpoint support for your cloud and region during scoping.


## Next steps for agent sovereignty


List every runtime call your agents make, with its destination, jurisdiction, and transfer tool. Close the gaps with default-deny egress, region policy, and proxy-held credentials before regulated data enters the pipeline.

## FAQs about network sovereignty for AI agents


### Does EU data residency make an AI agent GDPR-compliant?


EU data residency alone doesn't make an AI agent GDPR-compliant. Residency fixes where data is stored, but agents still send prompts and tool calls abroad. Each of those flows needs a transfer tool, such as an adequacy decision or SCCs. You also need evidence of the provider's ownership and staff access. Support staff accessing the data from outside the EEA triggers a transfer.


### Can I still rely on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for agent API calls?


Yes, for certified US recipients, as long as the adequacy decision remains in place. The framework faces an appeal at the EU Court of Justice and EDPB scrutiny of a US Supreme Court ruling. Keep SCCs and a transfer impact assessment drafted for critical US providers. If the adequacy decision changes, you can switch tools without halting production agents.


### Is private networking the same as an air-gapped deployment?


No. Private networking keeps traffic off the public internet through private endpoints or interconnects. An air-gapped deployment has no connection to an outside control plane. Blaxel's private networking and Bring Your Own Metal options both keep a link to its managed control plane. Ask each vendor what metadata and commands cross that control-plane link.
